summary.text: 放 combines 攵, an action-related component, with 方 as a sound component. Its transmitted early gloss is “expel” or “drive away”; “release” and “let go” are also recorded meanings.

formation.text: The traditional analysis is phonosemantic: 攴, appearing in this position as 攵, contributes an action-related meaning, while 方 supplies the sound. A later proposal that 方 also means “distant” here, or that 攴 specifically means admonition, is uncertain.

components.text: 攵 is the positional form of 攴 in this traditional analysis and contributes an action-related meaning. A more specific meaning of admonition has been proposed, but remains uncertain.
方 is the sound component in the traditional analysis. A further proposal that it contributes the meaning “distant” is not established.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison uses system-dependent reconstructions. It supports a plausible sound relationship but does not establish the precise original phonetic identity or pronunciation.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, 方 *paŋ (also *baŋ) compares with 放 *paŋ-s in its release reading. The shared *paŋ supports a plausible relationship; these reconstructions are not direct records of ancient speech.

history.text: The received Shuowen text glosses 放 as 逐, “expel” or “drive away,” and analyzes it as 攴 plus phonetic 方. A classical-text tradition records this banishing sense in a passage dated approximately to the fourth century BCE; that estimate does not date a surviving manuscript.

A Taiwan dictionary reports a Warring States Zhongshan Wang Hu form as a variant later regularized as 放. Its image was not visually examined, so the available account does not support describing its shape or specific changes to the graph.

uncertainties.text: The available accounts do not establish a securely dated earliest graphic occurrence, a complete sequence of ancient forms, or graphic corruption.
The reconstructed comparison makes 方 a plausible phonetic component, but it does not identify a depicted object or establish a whole-character borrowing account.

A scholarly proposal derives “reach” from “banish” or “send away,” drawing on Mencius passages and Han commentary. The development remains disputed, and a complete chronology linking older and modern senses is unresolved.

A distinct reading meaning “imitate” is recorded. Its chronology and historical relationship to the release reading are unresolved.

limitations.text: The chronology and semantic connections among “expel,” “release,” “reach,” “imitate,” and other recorded uses remain unresolved. In particular, the proposed development to “reach” is disputed.

Reconstructed pronunciations support a plausible component-level sound comparison but are not direct recordings of ancient speech. No supported whole-character phonetic loan explains the recorded meanings.

evidence.text: let go
Phonosemantic compound. 攵 represents the meaning and 方 represents the sound.
逐也。从攴方聲。凡放之屬皆从放。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *paŋʔ, *paŋs): phonetic 方 (OC *paŋ, *baŋ) + semantic 攵 (“hand, action”) – an action, release.
Compare Tibetan སྤོང (spong, “to abandon; to let go”), Burmese ဖင့် (hpang., “to delay”) (Hill, 2019).

For pronunciation and definitions of 放 – see 方 (“parallel; side by side; parallel boats; raft made of bamboo; etc.”).
(This character is a variant form of 方).

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, as transcribed in Hanyu Guoxue
evidence.text: The received 大徐本 entry says 放 means “逐” (expel/pursue) and analyzes it as 从攴、方聲. The page attributes this text to the Song recension of the Han dictionary. A later explanatory gloss on the page proposes that 方 also contributes “far”; that added semantic account is not part of the quoted Shuowen entry and is not independently established here.
evidence.title: 放的说文解字解释_放的说文解字原文

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry cites Shuowen’s 从攴，方聲 analysis and reports that the Guwenzi Leibi gives a Warring States Zhongshan Wang Hu form as an alternative graph, regularized later as a variant of 放. Its graphic forms are displayed as images and were not visually inspected here, so this supports the dictionary’s report but not a direct shape comparison. Its sources for the character’s historical forms are listed, but several are marked unavailable.
evidence.title: A01719 放 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The page labels 放 a phonosemantic compound and places it in the 方 phonetic series. For the release reading it gives Beijing Mandarin fàng, Middle Chinese pjangH in Baxter’s notation, and Old Chinese *paŋ-s in Baxter–Sagart 1.1; it gives Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese *paŋs. For the distinct ‘imitate’ reading it lists fǎng, pjangX, and *paŋʔ in Baxter–Sagart. 方 is listed with Old Chinese *paŋ, *baŋ in the page’s series table. These are reconstructions, not directly recorded ancient pronunciations. The comparison supports 方 as a plausible sound component; the reading-specific tones should not be collapsed into one form.
evidence.title: 放 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry lists Standard Mandarin fàng and Guangzhou/Hong Kong Cantonese Jyutping fong3 for the release sense. The dossier’s Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese and Tang readings were not independently checked against primary language-specific references in this research.
evidence.title: 放 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: Search results for its 放逐 entry reproduce the Shuowen gloss 放：逐也, but opening this page returned HTTP 403. This was not treated as independently inspected evidence.

evidence.source: Liu Xinyao, Beijing Normal University, conference abstract
evidence.text: The abstract reports three Mencius occurrences interpreted by Zhao Qi (Han) as ‘reach’: 放於琅邪, 放乎四海, and 摩頂放踵. It proposes that ‘reach’ developed from ‘banish/send away’ and explains 摩頂放踵 as extending from head to heel; it also argues that older witnesses support 摩頂放於踵. This is a scholar’s semantic proposal, not a settled derivation. It documents use and exegesis, but does not establish a first attestation date for the underlying word.
evidence.title: 上古漢語至到義“放”的句法語義分析——重論“摩頂放踵”（摘要）

evidence.text: The character page gives the passage 齊宣王問曰：「湯放桀，武王伐紂，有諸？」 under its ‘banish/exile’ sense, dated to approximately the 4th century BCE in the entry. This is evidence of the sense in a classical text tradition, but the date is approximate and is not an archaeological date for the surviving manuscript witnesses.
evidence.title: 放 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The page records modern senses including release/free, let out, place/set down, expand, distribute, and play a recording; it includes a 1949 example for ‘herd/put livestock out to pasture.’ These attest different later uses but do not establish a complete chronology or direct semantic links among them.
evidence.title: 放 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: Its modern explanatory section says 攴 originally denotes a small strike and suggests it refers here to instruction or admonition, while 方 is both phonetic and semantic, suggesting banishment to a distant place. This is an editorial interpretation beyond Shuowen’s explicit phonetic statement and lacks corroboration in the sources inspected; treat the component’s semantic role as uncertain. The core 攴 + 方聲 analysis is independently reported in Shuowen and the Taiwan Ministry of Education entry.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

Shuowen’s explicit account is phonetic 方 with semantic 攴 under its traditional analysis. The idea that 方 additionally means ‘distant’ and that 攴 specifically means admonition comes from later editorial commentary and was not independently verified.

The proposed phonetic role is independently plausible from the recorded historical readings (放 *paŋ-s / *paŋʔ versus 方 *paŋ, *baŋ in Baxter–Sagart presentation), but reconstructions are model-dependent. Zhengzhang *paŋs is also listed for the release reading. These data do not identify an original depicted object or imply a whole-graph loan.
The two readings/senses shown for 放 (*paŋʔ ‘imitate’; *paŋ-s ‘release’) should be kept distinct. Their exact historical relation and chronology were not established in the inspected sources.

Semantic extension from banish/release to ‘reach’ is a scholarly proposal supported by Han commentary and Mencius examples, not a proven chronological sequence. The path from ‘release’ to modern ‘put/place,’ launch, distribute, or other senses is not established by chronological evidence here.

No proposed whole-character phonetic loan was substantiated; the dossier’s comparisons with Tibetan and Burmese were not investigated as borrowing claims and should not be treated as proof of loan direction or source pronunciation.

The transmitted Shuowen analysis treats 攴 as the semantic element and 方 as phonetic. The further claim that 方 contributes ‘distant’ and 攴 means admonition is a later editorial interpretation, not established by the Shuowen wording inspected.

The proposed 方 sound role is supported by historical phonological comparisons in named reconstruction systems, with reading-specific differences for 放. The reconstructed sound does not identify an original depicted object, and no whole-graph phonetic-loan claim was substantiated.

Available textual dictionary examples include ‘expel/banish,’ ‘discard,’ ‘release,’ ‘open,’ ‘emit/shoot,’ and a fǎng reading with ‘imitate,’ ‘according to,’ and ‘reach.’ Those citations do not by themselves establish earliest attestations or a chronological semantic path. The proposed development of ‘reach’ from ‘banish/send away’ remains disputed.
No independently inspected primary evidence established the dossier’s Tibetan or Burmese comparisons as borrowing claims, their direction, early attestations, or the relevant source pronunciation.
